jobs.title: Canadian Financial and Regulatory Reporting, VP
jobs.description:
**Discover your future at Citi**
--------------------------------


Working at Citi is far more than just a job. A career with us means joining a team of approximately 219,000 dedicated people from around the globe. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact.


**Job Overview**
----------------


The Finance Reporting Lead Analyst is senior professional position responsible for driving the generation, analysis, and submission of reports to various constituencies based on requirements such as US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), US Regulatory, and local statutory reporting, in coordination with the broader Financial Reporting Team. The overall objective is to apply in\-depth disciplinary knowledge to contribute to directional strategy.
  

  

**Responsibilities:**


* Support the analysis and submission of reports to various constituencies (local regulators, SEC, Fed, OCC, etc.) based on requirements such as US GAAP, US Regulatory, and local statutory reporting
* Assist with closing the books and sub\-ledgers, including passing appropriate required adjustment entries and consolidating financials at the end of each accounting period
* Instill operational discipline into existing team processes
* Work with senior leadership on strategic planning, establishing guidelines, implementing controls, and executing strategic plans
* Mentor and advise on directional strategy by analyzing subject matter and its application within role and the business
* Assist with the implementation of policies and procedures
* Serve as a technical mentor for an area within the business
* Build and maintain a thorough understanding of related product reporting and analytics and utilize knowledge of systems and process flows to provide insight and recommendations on identified issues
* Has the ability to operate with a limited level of direct supervision.
* Can exercise independence of judgement and autonomy.
* Acts as SME to senior stakeholders and /or other team members.
* Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behavior, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency.
  

  

**Qualifications:**


* 6\-10 years of experience in Financial Services preferred
* Global Project Management experience preferred
* Ability to work under pressure and manage deadlines or unexpected changes in expectations or requirements
* Proven organizational and time management skills
* Proven problem\-solving and decision\-making skills
* Consistently demonstrates clear and concise written and verbal communication skills
  

  

**Education:**


* Bachelor’s Degree/University degree or equivalent experience
* Master’s degree preferred
  

  

This job description provides a high\-level review of the types of work performed. Other job\-related duties may be assigned as required.


\-


**Job Family Group:**
---------------------

Finance
\-


**Job Family:**
---------------


Financial Reporting
\-


**Time Type:**
--------------


Full time
\-


**Primary Location Full Time Salary Range:**
--------------------------------------------


$111,600\.00 \- $161,600\.00
\-


**Most Relevant Skills**
------------------------

Accounting Processes and Financial Controls, Assessment, Balance Sheet, Business Acumen, Constructive Debate, Data Analysis, Financial Reporting, Internal Controls, Process Design, Regulatory Management.
\-


**Other Relevant Skills**
-------------------------

For complementary skills, please see above and/or contact the recruiter.
\-


**Automated Processing and AI**
-------------------------------


We use automated processing, including artificial intelligence, for our legitimate business interests (or our reasonable and appropriate business purposes) to identify and align the candidate's skills and abilities with a specific job opening. Additionally, if you so choose, or consent, we can match your skills and abilities to other suitable roles at Citi.


Importantly, all our hiring processes and decisions, including determining your suitability for a role, are conducted, checked, and decided by individuals. Our automated processing and AI do not involve relying on automatic or autonomous decision\-making. Please refer to any Jurisdictional Considerations, with specific provisions for your country (where relevant) for further details.

jobs.title: Director of AI Delivery
jobs.description:
**The bright side of mortgages**


nesto is Canada's leading digital residential mortgage lender, offering Canadians the lowest rates from the get\-go – with total transparency and no haggling.

 **About Us**


As Canada's pioneer in online mortgage lending, nesto is transforming the way Canadians finance their homes. Our mission is to offer a positive, empowering, and transparent property financing experience, simplified from start to finish.

  

Borrowers benefit from rates that are often lower than those offered by the big banks, along with an exceptional end\-to\-end mortgage experience powered by best\-in\-class AI technology. Fast, simple, and fully digital, nesto has been recognized as CLA Lender of the Year for three consecutive years. That's the bright side of mortgages.

 **Nesto Group**


Nesto Group is Canada's leading provider of mortgage technology and financing solutions, with more than CAD $80 billion in residential and commercial mortgages under administration. Trusted by many of the country's leading financial institutions, we combine over 50 years of mortgage expertise with proprietary cloud and AI technology to transform the future of lending.

  

Powered by our proprietary cloud and AI technology, nesto has become one of Canada's fastest\-growing mortgage lenders, gaining market share across direct\-to\-consumer (D2C) residential lending, the broker channel, and multi\-family commercial lending. Recognized as one of Deloitte's Fast 50 companies for three consecutive years, we continue to push the industry forward through innovation, technology, and customer\-focused solutions.

  

Operating through our family of brands – CMLS, nesto, and Nesto Cloud – our mission is to build Canada's mortgage ecosystem of the future and create a true Canadian champion in lending technology and financial services. Learn more at: https://nestogroup.ca/

 **Work Location**


Hybrid, based in our Toronto or Montreal office. In\-office expectations vary with business needs. If you are based in Montreal, expect to travel to Toronto a couple of times per month.

 **Why We Are Hiring**


Maestro, our AI\-powered underwriting platform, already runs inside nesto, with AI agents making real\-time, policy\-based decisions. We are now bringing it to financial institution clients through Nesto Cloud. You will be the first leader of client AI delivery. Your mission is to run the program that puts a fleet of AI agents live in Canadian banks’ production environments. As our Director of AI Delivery, you'll own it end to end: the delivery plan, the pod, the day\-to\-day client relationship, and the evidence that moves each agent through requirements, testing, model\-risk approval, live\-file shadow, joint change management, and progressive production activation. You will also write the repeatable deployment playbook we reuse for every client that follows.

 **What You'll Be Doing**

* **Lead Maestro delivery.** Set a clear delivery approach amid uncertainty and build trust with client executives.
* **Own the plan and stage exits.** Own the plan across underwriting agents. Call each stage exit against its written proof point across our 9 stages: scoping, process mapping, golden sets, configuration, evaluation, model governance, shadow, change management, and progressive production decisioning.
* **Lead the pod.** Lead a senior delivery pod (delivery managers, underwriting expert, data scientists, program PM) day to day. Guide the AI Delivery Managers as they gather requirements for each agent. Work with the assigned PM and the relevant delivery and technical colleagues to keep implementations moving. Run standups and working sessions, and build and defend the steering narrative. The client Sponsor makes the final call on the story.
* **Chair eval review.** Run the weekly review of agent performance evidence and turn it into build and tuning priorities for Engineering. Data Scientists produce the evidence. You review it and do not produce it yourself.
* **Lead the model\-risk relationship.** Lead the relationship with the client’s model\-risk team. Land validation packages for each condition family and secure the risk and governance sign\-offs that authorize shadow and production.
* **Run the shadow program.** Adjudicate divergences, re\-validate for drift, and report value foregone to client executives each month.
* **Own change management and readiness.** Co\-own the joint readiness sign\-off with the client and make sure the pilot group is trained and running the new workflow.
* **Build the deployment playbook.** Write the repeatable process that takes AI agents from client requirements through testing and client approval into production. Document each agent’s deployment as you go. The playbook is a core deliverable, not a retrospective.
* **Protect scope.** Hold client “small asks” to the config log and SOW change process. Nothing gets absorbed silently.

 **What You Bring**

* You have a client\-facing delivery background, as an engagement manager, Delivery Director, or Implementation Director.
* You have run senior delivery teams on client sites and led working sessions with EVP\-level executives.
* You have led client AI implementations hands\-on, from requirements through production.
* You know ML/AI delivery well enough to chair an eval review, question precision and recall trade\-offs, and translate model evidence into language a risk committee can act on.
* You define written exit criteria, produce the artifacts that back them, and document decisions.

 **Nice\-to\-Have**

* Experience implementing AI for banks or other regulated organizations, including model\-risk validation.
* Experience implementing your own company’s product at the client.
* Mortgage or retail\-credit domain knowledge, or experience with staged production rollouts of decisioning systems.
* Comfort building the playbook while running it in a scale\-up.

 **This Role Might Be for You If**

* You have delivered AI solutio

jobs.title: Director Planning & Performance
jobs.description:
JOIN OUR TEAM
  
  

Metro Supply Chain is a strategic supply chain solutions partner to some of the world's fastest growing and most reputable organizations. For 50 years, it has excelled at tailoring integrated, data driven solutions, fueled by advanced systems and technology, that fulfill complex and challenging distribution needs. Managing 22\.5 million square feet operating out of more than 190 sites across North America and Europe with a team of 9,000, it is one of Canada's largest privately owned supply chain solutions companies. Metro Supply Chain is a 2026 winner of the Canada's Best Managed Companies program, recognized for its strategic expertise, culture of innovation and commitment to its people and local communities.
  
  

SUMMARY
  
The Director, Planning \& Performance leads Metro Supply Chain’s enterprise planning, forecasting, performance reporting, and long\-range financial planning processes. Partnering with the Executive Leadership Team, Business Unit leaders, and FP\&A, the role delivers integrated financial insights, identifies risks and opportunities, and enables informed strategic and operational decision\-making.
  
RESPONSIBILITIES
  
Business Planning \& Forecast
  
* Lead the development, consolidation, review, and ongoing monitoring of the annual Corporate Business Plan, quarterly forecasts, and multi\-year strategic financial plan.
* Establish enterprise planning assumptions, methodologies, timelines, templates, and governance requirements in partnership with Business Unit and functional leaders.
* Consolidate Business Unit plans and forecasts, assess completeness and reasonableness, and identify key risks, opportunities, dependencies, and performance gaps.
* Develop integrated three\- to five\-year financial projections, including income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, capital requirements, and scenario analysis aligned with corporate strategy.
* Lead enterprise capital budgeting and forecasting, providing visibility into investment priorities, timing, expected returns, funding requirements, and impacts on cash flow.
* Partner with Business Unit leaders and FP\&A to forecast new\-business growth, monitor pipeline health against strategic objectives, and assess the effects of timing, probability, and value changes on the annual plan and latest forecast.


Monthly Performance Reporting
  
* Lead the monthly business performance reporting cycle, consolidating actual results against budget, prior year, and latest forecast and delivering clear, decision\-oriented commentary on key revenue, cost, profitability, cash flow, and operational variances.
* Prepare concise executive reporting packages and performance narratives that translate financial and operational results into key business drivers, emerging risks, opportunities, and recommended management actions aligned with enterprise KPIs and strategic priorities.
* Perform monthly forecast\-to\-forecast bridge and impact analysis, quantifying movements from prior outlooks and explaining the underlying assumptions, timing differences, business drivers, and implications for full\-year performance.
* Coordinate closely with Business Unit leaders, Operations Finance, FP\&A, and other functional stakeholders to validate results, align commentary and forecasts, resolve data or reporting issues, and ensure timely, accurate, and consistent submissions.
* Maintain reporting controls, data\-validation standards, KPI definitions, and submission calendars to ensure management reporting is accurate, complete, consistent, and delivered within established deadlines.


Planning Process Excellence, Systems \& Continuous Improvement
  
* Assess the effectiveness of planning, forecasting, and reporting processes and maintain a prioritized improvement roadmap aligned with business needs and finance transformation objectives.
* Lead initiatives to simplify and standardize workflows, reduce cycle times, eliminate non\-value\-added activities, improve forecast accuracy, and increase the quality and timeliness of decision support.
* Standardized planning assumptions, templates, calendars, KPI definitions, documentation, and governance practices across Business Units.
* Partners with FP\&A, Business Units, Data Analytics, and Technology teams to enhance planning tools, automate recurring activities, improve system adoption, and strengthen data and reporting controls.
* Develop and monitor measures of process effectiveness, including forecast accuracy, reporting timeliness, data quality, user adoption, and completion of improvement initiatives.
* Document critical planning and reporting processes, establish sustainable controls, and provide training and guidance to stakeholders.
* Lead or support strategic finance initiatives, business cases, scenario analyses, and cross\-functional projects sponsored by the CFO, CEO, or Executive Leadership Team.
* Provide financial insight and analytical support for growth initiatives, investment decisions, productivity programs, organizational priorities, and emerging business requirements.
* Develop clear recommendations, implementation considerations, and executive materials to support timely decision\-making and accountability.


EXPERIENCE
  
* 8–10 years of progressive experience in FP\&A, corporate planning, commercial finance, or business performance management within a large, complex organization. Experience in third\-party logistics, supply chain, transportation, distribution, or another operationally intensive industry is strongly preferred.
* 5\+ years of experience leading cross\-functional teams, enterprise planning processes, and strategic initiatives, with or without formal direct\-report accountability.
* Demonstrated experience leading enterprise budgeting, forecasting, long\-range planning, management reporting, and performance analysis processes.
* Advanced proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, with experience using enterprise planning, ERP, and business intelligence platforms

jobs.title: AVP, Enterprise Digital Capabilities
jobs.description:
We are seeking a strategic, collaborative and product\-minded leader to join our team as Assistant Vice President (AVP), Enterprise Digital Capabilities. This role is a key leader in Manulife's multi\-year transformation to modernize and converge our digital ecosystem across Canada, the US, Asia and Global Wealth \& Asset Management.
  

  

At the heart of this role is a simple objective: identify what is common across our digital experiences, build it once as an enterprise capability, and enable markets and segments to reuse and extend it to accelerate their own digital roadmaps.
  

  

Manulife has established a strong portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities that support our Digital Storefront transformation and broader unification ambitions. The next opportunity is to expand and scale this portfolio to accelerate the unification strategies and roadmaps of our segments and advance One Manulife experiences across the enterprise. The AVP will lead this evolution – working across segments to identify where common capabilities can create the greatest incremental value, bringing together requirements to ensure capabilities are designed for enterprise reuse, defining adoption and rollout strategies, and establishing a federated model where capabilities can be developed globally or contributed by segments and scaled for broader enterprise benefit.
  

  

The AVP will own the strategy and evolution of this portfolio — identifying new opportunities for reuse, prioritizing investment, establishing strong product management disciplines, driving adoption, optimizing existing capabilities and ensuring that each enterprise investment continues to deliver measurable value.
  

  

A critical part of the role is leading the Common Capability Collective, bringing together digital and product leaders from across the enterprise to identify common needs, align roadmaps, determine where enterprise investment can eliminate duplication and accelerate delivery, and create a shared view of capability priorities.
  

  

This is an enablement role, not ownership of individual market or segment experiences. The AVP will partner closely with Digital Storefront and segment digital leaders to understand their roadmaps and determine how enterprise capabilities can help them deliver faster, with greater quality, consistency and efficiency.
  

  

The AVP will operate in a two\-in\-a\-box partnership with a complementary Global Technology leader, jointly shaping the business and technology evolution of enterprise digital capabilities. Together, they will ensure capabilities are scalable, secure, reusable, well\-integrated and designed for long\-term enterprise value.

  

  

**Position Responsibilities**
  

  

***Enterprise Capability Strategy \& Portfolio***  

  



* Own the strategy, roadmap and ongoing evolution of Manulife's portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities.
* Establish a clear view of the capabilities required to support digital convergence across markets, segments and channels.
* Continuously identify common business and customer needs that can be solved once and reused across the enterprise.
* Assess existing segment capabilities for opportunities to scale them globally rather than rebuilding equivalent solutions.
* Prioritize enterprise investment based on customer value, segment demand, reuse potential, strategic alignment and economic benefit.
* Maintain a multi\-year capability roadmap aligned to Digital Storefront, segment roadmaps and Manulife's broader digital strategy.
* Ensure the portfolio remains focused and sustainable by rationalizing overlapping capabilities, technology and licenses where appropriate.
  

  

  

***Common Capability Collective \& Federated Leadership***  

  



* Lead the Common Capability Collective, bringing together Digital Storefront and product leaders from across the enterprise to jointly shape capability priorities and investment.
* Create transparency across segment roadmaps to identify shared needs, opportunities for reuse and potential duplication before investment occurs.
* Establish a federated model that enables capabilities to originate within segments where appropriate and subsequently evolve into reusable enterprise capabilities.
* Build alignment around enterprise standards and shared capabilities while preserving segment accountability for their own customer experiences and business outcomes.

Create clear decision rights, funding principles, ownership models and governance for the creation and evolution of common capabilities.  
* 

***Product Management \& Capability Evolution***  

  



* Establish strong product management disciplines across the enterprise capability portfolio, including product vision, roadmaps, adoption, performance measurement and lifecycle management.
* Ensure every capability has clear customer and business outcomes, ownership, success measures and an evolution roadmap.
* Use segment feedback, performance data and emerging customer needs to continuously improve capabilities.
* Drive adoption and reuse across markets and segments, ensuring enterprise investments translate into meaningful acceleration of local roadmaps.
* Ensure capabilities are designed for extensibility so segments can meet differentiated market needs without unnecessarily duplicating core functionality.
* Manage capabilities through their full lifecycle, including investment, enhancement, optimization, consolidation and retirement.
  

  

***AI Enablement \& Optimization***  

  



* Establish an AI\-by\-default approach to the development and evolution of enterprise digital capabilities.
* Identify opportunities to embed AI directly into capabilities to improve customer experiences, decisioning, personalization and digital effectiveness.
* Apply AI and automation across the capability lifecycle to accelerate development, testing, implementation, operations and ongoing optimization.
* Partner with Technology and enterpris

jobs.title: VICE PRESIDENT, ANALYTICS & HEALTH OUTCOMES
jobs.description:
**WHO WE ARE**


GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non\-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. We believe health care is a right, not a privilege, and we are committed to improving health outcomes, advancing health equity, and building a future where every Canadian can reach their full health and well\-being potential.


Through our unique integrated payer\-provider ("payvider") model, we offer insurance, administer benefits, and pay claims as a ‘payer’ while offering health care services such as mental health, pharmacy, telemedicine, and chronic disease management as a ‘provider’. As a non\-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well\-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025\. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.


At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

**THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL**


Reporting to the SVP, Product, Experience \& Health Outcomes, the Vice President, Analytics and Health Outcomes is a strategic senior leadership role responsible for turning GreenShield’s data into actionable insights, measurable outcomes, and clear narratives that inform priorities, support decision\-making, and demonstrate impact. This leader will work across the organization to connect analytics and insights to enterprise priorities and measurable impact in a way that helps leaders understand what is happening, why it matters, and where to act.


This role will be responsible for:

* Lead enterprise analytics and outcomes capabilities, ensuring data is used to inform priorities, guide investment decisions, and measure impact across the enterprise.
* Translate complex data into clear insights, narratives, and recommendations that help executives, product teams, clinical leaders, clients, and partners understand where to act and how to create measurable value.
* Build scalable measurement practices that help GreenShield assess performance, outcomes, and impact across its portfolio.
* Develop clear, evidence\-based insights for internal and external stakeholders to demonstrate impact.  

Partner cross\-functionally to embed analytics and outcome measures into planning, decision\-making, client insights, and performance management.
* Use data\-driven insights to support better experiences, decisions, and outcomes.
* Provide thought leadership on data quality, governance, privacy, responsible AI, and scalable analytics practices, working closely with Technology and enterprise data teams to ensure the right data foundations are in place.
* Build and lead a high\-performing team that combines analytical depth, business judgment, storytelling, and a practical orientation toward measurable outcomes.

 **WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR**

  

* 15\+ years of progressive analytics experience in health care, benefits, insurance, consulting, or a related field, including senior leadership accountability for analytics, insight generation, and business impact.
* Proven ability to turn data into insight, insight into action, and action into measurable business, customer, and health outcomes.
* Exceptional storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis into simple, credible, executive\-ready narratives for internal leaders, clients, partners, and external audiences.
* Business\-oriented analytics leader who can ask the right questions, define the right measures, challenge assumptions, and connect data to decisions that improve performance and impact.
* Experience building outcome frameworks, dashboards, scorecards, insights, analytics products, or executive reporting that drive decision\-making.
* Advanced analytics expertise, including predictive modelling, segmentation, measurement design, statistical analysis, data visualization, and practical application to business, customer, and health outcome questions.
* Strong advanced analytics capability, including familiarity with AI and machine learning applications.
* A collaborative, practical, and outcomes\-focused leadership style, with the ability to operate at both strategic and execution levels in a fast\-moving environment.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Base Salary:** Range exempt

**Offer positioning:** Determined using relevant experience, skills, internal equity and current market data.  

**Additional compensation:** Eligible for a discretionary target bonus.  

**Total rewards:** Health and dental coverage, retirement savings, paid time off and well\-being support (up to $10,000 per year for mental health).  

**Posting disclosures:** This is for an existing vacancy.  

**Work model:** Hybrid

**THE CULTURE**  

We believe a career should be meaningful. Not just a means to earn a living. Our culture is one where everyone's voice is heard and valued. Because that’s what it takes to create better health for all. We dare to challenge the status quo. And we’re driven by people who have challenged theirs. We believe that your workplace should empower you to be the best version of yourself. That’s why we provide a place where you can be inspired, challenged, and rewarded.  

  

Where your growth means our growth.  

Where your voice is heard and valued.  

Where your work has purpose. And purpose matters.

**Date Posted**: 10/26/2026


**Job Details**:


**Company Description:**

  

  

  

Core\-Mark continues to grow as the industry leader in fresh and broadline solutions for the convenience retail industry. With a reputation for empowering customers, employees, and communities, Core\-Mark has become the largest, most comprehensive marketer of consumer goods in North America \- offering a full range of products, programs, and solutions to convenience operators across the U.S. and Canada.  

  

  

**Job Description:**


**We Deliver the Goods:**
* Competitive pay and benefits, including Health \& Wellness Benefits, Employee Stock Purchase Plan, RRSP, Paid Direct Drug Card, \& Scholarship Opportunities for children of associates, Paid Time Off, and much more
* Growth opportunities performing essential work to support North America's food distribution system
* Safe and inclusive working environment, including culture of rewards, recognition, and respect

  

**Regional Finance Director \- Position Summary**
  

The Regional Finance Director leads the financial strategy and performance for the Canada \& 3PL Region, overseeing multiple sites and finance teams. This role is responsible for financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cost management, compliance, operational finance, and supporting strategic business decisions. The position partners closely with operational leadership to drive financial performance and ensure strong financial controls across the region.
  

  

**Key Responsibilities**
* Lead financial oversight for multiple locations within the region.
* Ensure accurate financial reporting and integrity of financial statements.
* Develop and manage annual budgets, forecasts, and financial plans.
* Monitor financial performance and identify cost\-saving opportunities.
* Provide financial analysis and recommendations to support business strategy and operational decisions.
* Ensure compliance with company policies, financial controls, and regulatory requirements.
* Lead, mentor, and develop regional finance teams.
Support financial aspects of acquisitions, startups, integrations, and business changes.  
* 

  

  

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or related field
* 7 \- 10 Years of related experience
* 1 \- 3 Years of supervisory or management experience
* Extensive experience in finance, accounting, or a related field.
* Proven track record in a leadership role, managing financial operations across multiple locations or regions.
* Strong analytical and strategic planning skills.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate with various stakeholders.
* Proficiency in financial software and tools, such as ERP systems.
* Knowledge of financial regulations and compliance requirements.
* Ability to lead, mentor, and develop finance teams across different regions.
* Experience in fostering a culture of collaboration and accountability.

  

**Preferred qualifications:**

* Master's Degree/MBA
* 10\+ Years of supervisory or management experience
* Certified Public Accountant (CPA)
* Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)

jobs.title: Director, Strategic Planning
jobs.description:
#### Description

The Director, Strategic Planning is responsible for leading the company's strategic direction in Canada, overseeing corporate strategy, product planning, commercial performance, digital mobility, and regulatory readiness. The role translates global objectives into Canadian market strategies to drive growth, profitability, competitiveness, and long\-term business success.


Responsibilities
----------------

**1\. Strategic Planning \& Business Performance**


* Lead Canadian strategic planning, annual business plans, and long\-term business priorities.
* Advise executive leadership on market trends, growth opportunities, profitability, and competitive positioning.
* Oversee strategic budgets, investments, business cases, and performance metrics.
* Identify business opportunities, assess risks, and drive strategic initiatives.
**2\. Product Planning \& Commercial Strategy**


* Lead product portfolio strategy, vehicle positioning, pricing, specifications, and lifecycle planning.
* Oversee competitive analysis, customer insights, and residual value strategies.
* Align product strategies with Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Aftersales objectives.
* Collaborate with Global and Regional Headquarters on product strategies and launches.
* Assess electrification, emerging technologies, and new mobility opportunities.
**3\. Connected Vehicle Services \& Digital Mobility**


* Oversee connected vehicle services, digital platforms, and mobility strategies to drive adoption, customer engagement, and recurring revenue.
* Lead Canadian strategic planning for global initiatives, including OneApp implementation.
* Oversee digital infrastructure investments, including approximately $7 million in estimated fixed asset investments.
* Ensure appropriate governance of customer data privacy, payment information, vendor relationships, and contractual risks.
**4\. Regulatory Strategy \& Emerging Business**


* Lead strategic planning for Canadian automotive regulations, including Zero\-Emission Vehicle (ZEV) mandates.
* Assess regulatory exposure and develop compliance and risk mitigation strategies.
* Lead business readiness for emerging product categories, including Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) launches.
* Evaluate the business impact of electrification, charging solutions, and evolving regulatory requirements.
**5\. Leadership \& Stakeholder Management**


* Lead and develop the Strategic Planning \& Product Planning function, establishing priorities and performance objectives.
* Drive cross\-functional alignment across Sales, Marketing, Aftersales, Finance, IT, and Legal.
* Represent Canadian market priorities with Global and Regional Headquarters.
* Present strategic recommendations, investment proposals, and business performance to executive leadership.
* Manage key external partnerships and strategic vendor relationships.
Skills / Knowledge / Experience / Education Required
----------------------------------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Commerce, Economics, Engineering, or a related field; MBA preferred.
* 10–15\+ years of progressive automotive industry experience in strategic planning, product planning, or commercial strategy.
* Proven experience leading strategic initiatives, product portfolios, and cross\-functional projects.
* Strong knowledge of the Canadian automotive market, pricing, residual values, electrification, and regulatory requirements.
* Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, investment evaluation, and business case development.
* Excellent strategic thinking, leadership, analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
* Power BI and SAP experience are an asset.
Key Competencies
----------------

* Strategic leadership and business acumen
* Product and commercial strategy
* Financial and investment management
* Executive communication and stakeholder influence
* Cross\-functional and global collaboration
* Regulatory and risk management
* Innovation and customer focus

new_jobs.title: Director Planning & Performance
new_jobs.description:
JOIN OUR TEAM
  
  

Metro Supply Chain is a strategic supply chain solutions partner to some of the world's fastest growing and most reputable organizations. For 50 years, it has excelled at tailoring integrated, data driven solutions, fueled by advanced systems and technology, that fulfill complex and challenging distribution needs. Managing 22\.5 million square feet operating out of more than 190 sites across North America and Europe with a team of 9,000, it is one of Canada's largest privately owned supply chain solutions companies. Metro Supply Chain is a 2026 winner of the Canada's Best Managed Companies program, recognized for its strategic expertise, culture of innovation and commitment to its people and local communities.
  
  

SUMMARY
  
The Director, Planning \& Performance leads Metro Supply Chain’s enterprise planning, forecasting, performance reporting, and long\-range financial planning processes. Partnering with the Executive Leadership Team, Business Unit leaders, and FP\&A, the role delivers integrated financial insights, identifies risks and opportunities, and enables informed strategic and operational decision\-making.
  
RESPONSIBILITIES
  
Business Planning \& Forecast
  
* Lead the development, consolidation, review, and ongoing monitoring of the annual Corporate Business Plan, quarterly forecasts, and multi\-year strategic financial plan.
* Establish enterprise planning assumptions, methodologies, timelines, templates, and governance requirements in partnership with Business Unit and functional leaders.
* Consolidate Business Unit plans and forecasts, assess completeness and reasonableness, and identify key risks, opportunities, dependencies, and performance gaps.
* Develop integrated three\- to five\-year financial projections, including income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, capital requirements, and scenario analysis aligned with corporate strategy.
* Lead enterprise capital budgeting and forecasting, providing visibility into investment priorities, timing, expected returns, funding requirements, and impacts on cash flow.
* Partner with Business Unit leaders and FP\&A to forecast new\-business growth, monitor pipeline health against strategic objectives, and assess the effects of timing, probability, and value changes on the annual plan and latest forecast.


Monthly Performance Reporting
  
* Lead the monthly business performance reporting cycle, consolidating actual results against budget, prior year, and latest forecast and delivering clear, decision\-oriented commentary on key revenue, cost, profitability, cash flow, and operational variances.
* Prepare concise executive reporting packages and performance narratives that translate financial and operational results into key business drivers, emerging risks, opportunities, and recommended management actions aligned with enterprise KPIs and strategic priorities.
* Perform monthly forecast\-to\-forecast bridge and impact analysis, quantifying movements from prior outlooks and explaining the underlying assumptions, timing differences, business drivers, and implications for full\-year performance.
* Coordinate closely with Business Unit leaders, Operations Finance, FP\&A, and other functional stakeholders to validate results, align commentary and forecasts, resolve data or reporting issues, and ensure timely, accurate, and consistent submissions.
* Maintain reporting controls, data\-validation standards, KPI definitions, and submission calendars to ensure management reporting is accurate, complete, consistent, and delivered within established deadlines.


Planning Process Excellence, Systems \& Continuous Improvement
  
* Assess the effectiveness of planning, forecasting, and reporting processes and maintain a prioritized improvement roadmap aligned with business needs and finance transformation objectives.
* Lead initiatives to simplify and standardize workflows, reduce cycle times, eliminate non\-value\-added activities, improve forecast accuracy, and increase the quality and timeliness of decision support.
* Standardized planning assumptions, templates, calendars, KPI definitions, documentation, and governance practices across Business Units.
* Partners with FP\&A, Business Units, Data Analytics, and Technology teams to enhance planning tools, automate recurring activities, improve system adoption, and strengthen data and reporting controls.
* Develop and monitor measures of process effectiveness, including forecast accuracy, reporting timeliness, data quality, user adoption, and completion of improvement initiatives.
* Document critical planning and reporting processes, establish sustainable controls, and provide training and guidance to stakeholders.
* Lead or support strategic finance initiatives, business cases, scenario analyses, and cross\-functional projects sponsored by the CFO, CEO, or Executive Leadership Team.
* Provide financial insight and analytical support for growth initiatives, investment decisions, productivity programs, organizational priorities, and emerging business requirements.
* Develop clear recommendations, implementation considerations, and executive materials to support timely decision\-making and accountability.


EXPERIENCE
  
* 8–10 years of progressive experience in FP\&A, corporate planning, commercial finance, or business performance management within a large, complex organization. Experience in third\-party logistics, supply chain, transportation, distribution, or another operationally intensive industry is strongly preferred.
* 5\+ years of experience leading cross\-functional teams, enterprise planning processes, and strategic initiatives, with or without formal direct\-report accountability.
* Demonstrated experience leading enterprise budgeting, forecasting, long\-range planning, management reporting, and performance analysis processes.
* Advanced proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, with experience using enterprise planning, ERP, and business intelligence platforms

new_jobs.title: VICE PRESIDENT, ANALYTICS & HEALTH OUTCOMES
new_jobs.description:
**WHO WE ARE**


GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non\-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. We believe health care is a right, not a privilege, and we are committed to improving health outcomes, advancing health equity, and building a future where every Canadian can reach their full health and well\-being potential.


Through our unique integrated payer\-provider ("payvider") model, we offer insurance, administer benefits, and pay claims as a ‘payer’ while offering health care services such as mental health, pharmacy, telemedicine, and chronic disease management as a ‘provider’. As a non\-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well\-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025\. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.


At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

**THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL**


Reporting to the SVP, Product, Experience \& Health Outcomes, the Vice President, Analytics and Health Outcomes is a strategic senior leadership role responsible for turning GreenShield’s data into actionable insights, measurable outcomes, and clear narratives that inform priorities, support decision\-making, and demonstrate impact. This leader will work across the organization to connect analytics and insights to enterprise priorities and measurable impact in a way that helps leaders understand what is happening, why it matters, and where to act.


This role will be responsible for:

* Lead enterprise analytics and outcomes capabilities, ensuring data is used to inform priorities, guide investment decisions, and measure impact across the enterprise.
* Translate complex data into clear insights, narratives, and recommendations that help executives, product teams, clinical leaders, clients, and partners understand where to act and how to create measurable value.
* Build scalable measurement practices that help GreenShield assess performance, outcomes, and impact across its portfolio.
* Develop clear, evidence\-based insights for internal and external stakeholders to demonstrate impact.  

Partner cross\-functionally to embed analytics and outcome measures into planning, decision\-making, client insights, and performance management.
* Use data\-driven insights to support better experiences, decisions, and outcomes.
* Provide thought leadership on data quality, governance, privacy, responsible AI, and scalable analytics practices, working closely with Technology and enterprise data teams to ensure the right data foundations are in place.
* Build and lead a high\-performing team that combines analytical depth, business judgment, storytelling, and a practical orientation toward measurable outcomes.

 **WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR**

  

* 15\+ years of progressive analytics experience in health care, benefits, insurance, consulting, or a related field, including senior leadership accountability for analytics, insight generation, and business impact.
* Proven ability to turn data into insight, insight into action, and action into measurable business, customer, and health outcomes.
* Exceptional storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis into simple, credible, executive\-ready narratives for internal leaders, clients, partners, and external audiences.
* Business\-oriented analytics leader who can ask the right questions, define the right measures, challenge assumptions, and connect data to decisions that improve performance and impact.
* Experience building outcome frameworks, dashboards, scorecards, insights, analytics products, or executive reporting that drive decision\-making.
* Advanced analytics expertise, including predictive modelling, segmentation, measurement design, statistical analysis, data visualization, and practical application to business, customer, and health outcome questions.
* Strong advanced analytics capability, including familiarity with AI and machine learning applications.
* A collaborative, practical, and outcomes\-focused leadership style, with the ability to operate at both strategic and execution levels in a fast\-moving environment.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Base Salary:** Range exempt

**Offer positioning:** Determined using relevant experience, skills, internal equity and current market data.  

**Additional compensation:** Eligible for a discretionary target bonus.  

**Total rewards:** Health and dental coverage, retirement savings, paid time off and well\-being support (up to $10,000 per year for mental health).  

**Posting disclosures:** This is for an existing vacancy.  

**Work model:** Hybrid

**THE CULTURE**  

We believe a career should be meaningful. Not just a means to earn a living. Our culture is one where everyone's voice is heard and valued. Because that’s what it takes to create better health for all. We dare to challenge the status quo. And we’re driven by people who have challenged theirs. Where your voice is heard and valued.  

Where your work has purpose. And purpose matters.
